post.subtitle:
Why does modifying one part of your code break five unrelated things? You need the SOLID principles! Starting with Single Responsibility: a class should have only one reason to change. 🛠️

Learn how to master SOLID Principles Explained in this quick breakdown.

📖 Read the full guide here:
https://www.abstractalgorithms.dev/

In this Short:
- Why does modifying one part of your code break five unrelated things? You need SOLID!
- Open-Closed: extend without modifying. Liskov: subclasses shouldn't break parent behavior.
- Interface Segregation: split bloated interfaces. Dependency Inversion: depend on abstractions.
- Instead of a bloated helper class, split responsibilities into modular abstractions.
- Read the full guide in the description and subscribe for more coding tips!
